core_obligations: Set V to the complement of T and W to U cap V, and note that U and V cover X (proof lines 8310-8311).

Prove part (1): restricting the derived pushforward of the restriction of E to V gives the pushforward of E restricted to W, which vanishes because E vanishes on W, while restricting to U gives E back (proof lines 8312-8316).
Prove part (2): the derived pushforward of F vanishes on V and the extension by zero also vanishes on V, while on U both agree with F (proof lines 8317-8323).
proof_roadmap: Part (1) by restriction to U and V (proof lines 8312-8316).
Part (2) by the same two restrictions (proof lines 8317-8323).
difficulty_reason: For an open subspace j: U to X and a closed subset T of X contained in U, the lemma shows that an object of the derived category whose cohomology sheaves are supported on T is unchanged by the derived pushforward of its restriction to U, and that for an object of the derived category of U supported on T the extension by zero and the derived pushforward agree (statement lines 8297-8307). The proof sets V to the complement of T and W to U cap V, so that X is the union of the two opens U and V, and then checks the two assertions by restricting to U and to V: on V both the derived pushforward and the extension by zero vanish because the objects restrict to zero there, while on U both agree with the original object (proof lines 8309-8323). The restriction formula for the pushforward of a restriction along an open immersion is the single cited input. The claim is H2: a short two-open localization argument in which the closedness of T is exactly what makes the complement an open on which everything vanishes.
